what: One card is divided into several cells (usually three), and each cell holds the header of its destination page, built at that page’s size and scaled down to 1/3. When a cell is pressed, the triple-size version inside the card scales up threefold (1s cubic-bezier(.54,.15,.15,1)), the cell widths change from their own widths like 43·33·24% to equal divisions, and it is pulled up by the card’s top offset. The moment the pressed cell exactly covers the screen, it navigates to that address. Returning to the card in the same tab starts with that cell spread to screen size and shrinks back into the card in 1s cubic-bezier(.85,0,.45,.85). On hover, the thumbnail inside a cell recedes to .98 over .5s. Below 1024 the cells stack vertically and expand vertically.

options.back: Stem on return, default on — 0 turns it off
options.[data-fx-part=scale]: 1/3-reduced frame that fills the card — contains one stretcher inside
options.[data-fx-part=stretcher]: Triple-width panel — holds the cells (landscape at 1024 and above, portrait below)
options.[data-fx-part=column]: Field — the address that goes inside <a href> One and [data-fx-part=mini] (miniature of that page header). At 1024 and up, column width is set in the consuming css (same by default)
options.--fx-progress: Turns on the card as 1 (card) ↔ 0 (page) — for matching the thumbnail’s text size and margins with calc
options.Event: fx:card-zoom-page { index, href, dir: in } — Unfolding begins

note: The original (Brand site) scales this panel up inside a barba transition and swaps it with the next page — the part goes to its address at the moment it is fully expanded, so the next page’s first screen must match the thumbnail to look continuous. If the column count is not three, set the panel width to columns × screen.
